decisions.executionNote: Begin a slow elbow-up approach to the purple nut with the left arm, opening maintained; staging above table before vertical grasp.
Complete downward wrist orientation while approaching above the purple nut. Keep lateral separation and elbow-up continuity.
Lower above the purple nut for a close visual alignment check before closing; grasp offset remains uncertain.
Correct purple nut centering from wrist RGB, close fully, and make a short test lift to check retention.
Purple nut appears retained between jaws. Lift clear and carry within the left workspace toward its matching upright screw.
Lower the retained purple nut toward screw height and correct the visible lateral offset; pause near insertion height for wrist alignment.
Retry corrected tensor; the rejected chunk moved nothing. Shift the retained purple nut laterally toward the screw axis and inspect.
The purple nut is no longer centered between the jaws. Release and lift clear to inspect its resting position before a controlled regrasp.
Park the left arm clear of the displaced purple nut. Begin an elbow-up approach with the right arm toward the blue nut, maintaining open jaws.
Complete the right-arm top-down approach above the blue nut, using small continuous rotations and keeping left parked.
Descend with open right jaws toward the blue nut, correcting the small wrist tilt and pausing to inspect centering before grasp.
Center the blue nut using head and wrist geometry, close the right gripper fully, then make a small vertical retention test.
Blue nut appears retained and centered. Lift clear and transport it above the matching blue screw in the right workspace, keeping the gripper closed.
Lower the centered blue nut slowly toward the blue screw, holding orientation and closed jaws; inspect engagement before turning.
The blue screw appears slightly left of the nut opening. Lift a small clearance, correct laterally, and lower gently to engagement height.
Refine the remaining blue-axis offset and begin a slow clockwise tightening stroke with a very small downward feed. Monitor retention and seating.
Use the changed wrist view to refine blue screw alignment, then continue a short clockwise stroke with conservative axial feed.
Open the right jaws and reset the wrist for another tightening stroke, keeping the blue pair undisturbed at the same height. Check whether the nut remains seated.
Blue nut did not remain seated. Approach its visible resting position with open jaws for regrasp, avoiding the adjacent screw.
Center and regrasp the upright blue nut with a slow final descent, then lift slightly to verify retention.
Adjacent screw may obstruct a jaw. Open, lift, change the right gripper azimuth, and approach the blue nut again from a clearer jaw direction.
Close around the blue nut at the changed jaw angle, then test retention with a slow vertical lift before transporting.
The blue nut is now visibly retained. Raise it clear of the screw, then translate toward the screw axis while maintaining this grasp.
Use the screw's wrist-image axis to correct sideways offset, then descend slowly with the retained blue nut toward engagement.
Make a small in-plane correction for the nut's offset within the jaws, then lower five millimeters to seek coaxial engagement without forcing.
Correct the remaining apparent axis offset with a small horizontal motion only; keep the blue nut retained and inspect before additional insertion or rotation.
The previous correction moved the screw toward the nut axis. Continue that measured direction a few millimeters and lower gently, retaining the nut for an engagement check.
Begin a slow clockwise threading stroke, compensating approximately for the nut's offset in the jaws and using only slight axial feed. Engagement remains visually uncertain.
Continue a controlled clockwise stroke around the estimated blue nut axis with light downward position feed; keep both arm configurations continuous.
Release after the clockwise stroke and withdraw vertically a short distance to verify whether the blue nut is supported on the screw before regrasping.
The blue nut remains upright on the screw after release. Reset the open wrist and approach its supported position for another clockwise tightening stroke.
The regrasp tilted the blue nut. Open and lift slightly, then recenter from the wrist image before attempting another grasp; do not torque the tilted nut.
Approach the blue nut with fully open jaws, close at a centered pose, and make a short test lift to inspect its actual retention and attitude before any torque.
Blue nut now appears more upright around the screw. Open and approach its actual supported height, correcting the wrist-image offset before closing for tightening.
Blue nut is upright and the screw tip is visible within its bore. Close at this centered height, then apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial feed and small pivot compensation.
Continue the blue nut's clockwise tightening with a small axial feed, then release at the same pose to check that the aligned pair remains seated.
The blue nut remains upright on the screw after release. Reset the open wrist and reclose gently at the supported nut height for another tightening stroke.
Apply another slow clockwise tightening stroke to the upright blue nut with only two millimeters total downward feed, then release for visual verification.
Blue nut appears deeply seated and remains upright after release. Withdraw the open right gripper and approach the displaced purple nut with the left arm for regrasp.
Blue pair stays seated with its screw tip nearly flush. Lift left clear of the sideways purple nut; approach the upright gray nut with the right arm for a center-table transfer.
Center the right gripper over the upright gray nut, correct the small wrist tilt, descend slowly to grasp height, and close fully before a retention test.
Lift the gray nut and carry it slowly to the center handover area, with the left arm parked clear and the right gripper fully closed; inspect retention before placement.
Gray nut remains retained. Set it upright in the center handover area, open only after lowering to the table, then withdraw vertically before the left arm approaches.
The gray nut rests upright in the center. Withdraw the right arm to its own side, then bring the open left gripper toward the handover area while preserving arm separation.
Approach the upright gray nut in the center with the left arm; descend with open jaws while keeping the right arm parked safely in its workspace.
Make a small centering correction over the gray nut, close the left gripper fully at table grasp height, and lift sixteen millimeters to check retention.
Gray nut is visibly retained by the left jaws. Lift clear and carry it above the matching gray screw in the left workspace, keeping the right arm parked.
Lower the retained gray nut toward its matching screw with a small lateral centering correction. Pause near engagement height before applying torque.
Gray nut meets the screw off-axis. Lift slightly to unload the contact, make a small lateral correction, and return gently to the observed contact height without tightening yet.
Use the observed wrist-image response to reverse the lateral error and bring the gray screw toward the nut bore, retaining a small clearance during the horizontal correction.
The gray screw now appears centered behind the nut bore. Lower gently into engagement and begin a slow clockwise stroke with minimal axial feed, keeping the grasp closed.
Release and reset the left wrist without translating the gray pair, then reclose gently for another clockwise threading stroke; seating remains under visual inspection.
The gray bore still looks offset from the screw tip. Unload slightly, make a measured in-plane correction along the remaining axis error, and return gently without torque.
Apply a controlled clockwise gray-nut stroke around its estimated offset in the jaws, with a small axial feed. Release at the end to inspect whether the nut is supported coaxially on the screw.
Gray nut remains near the screw after release but its seating is uncertain. Lift the open jaws, reset the wrist, and center over the estimated nut axis before regrasping.
Gray nut is visibly back on the table beside its screw. Approach its actual resting position and change jaw azimuth to avoid the adjacent screw during regrasp.
Center over the gray nut using its visible bore, close at table grasp height, and make a short vertical retention test while avoiding the neighboring screw.
The gray nut appears retained. Lift vertically clear of the screw before attempting any lateral alignment, preserving the grasp and elbow-up configuration.
Transport the retained gray nut toward the visually located screw axis, then descend partway with clearance for a fresh alignment check.
Advance the gray nut along the remaining wrist-image axis error, then lower eleven millimeters slowly to seek coaxial engagement before turning.
Refine the remaining gray-axis offset and lower slowly to seat the nut. Release and withdraw slightly to verify support on the screw before further tightening.
The gray nut remains supported near the screw after release. Recenter over its observed position and close gently at the supported height before attempting a tightening stroke.
The gray nut was displaced by the attempted regrasp. Open and withdraw vertically, allowing it to settle before locating it for recovery.
Move the open left gripper toward the gray nut's new resting location, using wrist-relative geometry and pausing above it to refine alignment.
The gray nut is now clearly visible upright on the table. Refine its head-camera position and descend with open left jaws to grasp height, staying clear of the screw.
Close around the centered upright gray nut at table height, then lift vertically to confirm retention before moving toward the screw.
Gray nut is centered and retained in the new grasp. Lift clear, translate above the visually estimated gray screw axis, and approach slowly while keeping the gripper closed.
The gray screw tip is visible at the upper edge of the bore. Maintain the centered horizontal pose and lower slowly to engagement height before deciding on any lateral correction or torque.
The gray screw tip is now centered within the nut bore. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial feed, then open without moving the pair to verify seating.
Gray nut remains upright and coaxial after release. Reset the open left wrist at fixed position and reclose gently for the next tightening stroke.
Continue clockwise tightening of the centered gray nut with a small downward feed, then release at the same pose to verify the seated pair.
Gray nut appears deeply seated with the jaws open. Withdraw and reset the left wrist, then approach above the sideways purple nut for orientation recovery; keep the completed blue pair undisturbed.
Approach the purple nut on its side with open left jaws aligned across its broad faces. Pause at grasp height before attempting a controlled lift and reorientation.
Close on the purple nut's broad faces and lift vertically clear of its neighboring screw. Verify retention before changing the nut's attitude.
Purple nut is retained on its side. Begin a slow 45-degree reorientation in clear left-side space, maintaining the grip and elbow-up continuity; inspect before completing the roll.
Purple nut remains retained through the first half of the roll. Complete its upright reorientation slowly while carrying it to clear left-side space for a controlled set-down.
Replan from the interrupted pose: back away slightly from the wrist singularity, then lower the nearly upright purple nut toward a clear set-down area with the grasp maintained.

The last attempt executed zero steps. Retrace a small portion of the accepted roll-and-translation path to leave the near-singular wrist posture, then test a slow descent while retaining the purple nut.
